DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 08 s. 2021 3 February 2021 HON. MYCA ELIZABETH R. VERGARA City Mayor Cabanatuan City Nueva Ecija Dear Mayor Vergara: This refers to your letter dated 27 April 2020, requesting for the Department's legal opinion on whether or not an ordinance of a component city may be declared invalid by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on grounds other than being beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod. The grounds made by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is that, the provisions of Ordinance No. 026- 202 passed by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cabanatuan City contains technical infirmities, viz: 1. Curfew hours of 5PM to 5AM is contrary to the guidelines and advisories issued by the DILG; 2. The setting of market hours from 5AM to 1 IAM and 1 IAM to 4PM is a direct contravention of the advisory of DILG Secretary Ario on March 25, 2020; 3. On the schedule of other municipalities and other cities within the Province of Nueva Ecija and non-residents of the Province to enter Cabanatuan City will impair the right of the individual to obtain food and medicine in the City; 4. The ordinance directed the blockade of barangay tertiary roads with soil which in a sense is a permanent obstruction of the said road; 5. The ordinance provides that the quarantine pass will be for one time use only which defeat the very purpose of quarantine.

Hence, your request. Foremost, we would like to inform you that the Department has been very consistent in its previous legal opinions that the review power of Sangguniang Panlalawigan over ordinances is confined to Section 56(c) of the Local Government Code, to wit: "SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. — (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the Sanggunian Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan shall forward to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attomey, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) Ifthe Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. " xxx This has been bolstered in the case of Moday vs. Court of Appeals, where the Supreme Court, citing Velazco vs. Blas, held that: "The only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance, or order is beyond the powers conferred upon the council or president making the same. Absolutely no other ground is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers

conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limit, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council or president. Such has been the consistent course of executive authority. " Clearly, if the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecija finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part Nevertheless, to our mind, Ordinance No. 026-2020 passed by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cabanatuan City is within the powers coferred upon them by law, except for the provision on directing the blockade of barangay tertiary roads with soil. Hence, on the said technical infirmities, we find them consistent with the issuances issued by the National Government except for your justification/argument in number 4. It is our view that the setting up of checkpoints and barricades with the use of soil in barangay tertiary roads to regulate ingress-egress of residents is not in accordance with the implementing standards and not within the parameters of the community quarantine set by the National Government as the same may lead to loss of lives of patients in case/s of emergency/ies. You may put barriers, provided that, it has to be manned by authorized officials. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. CC: Dir. Julie J. Daquioag BY A OIC- n Very truly yours, RITY OF THE SECRETARY: NGAN , CESO Ill retary for Local Government Regional Director, DILG-Region Ill Secretary to the Sanggunian Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecija Ls/90
